name: Steve Hanke
zh_summary: My take in @eldiario with Francisco Zalles on the dollarization of Ecuador: The Ecuadorian sucre lost 75.6% of its value against the US dollar from 1998 until Jan. 2000, economy imploded. Since dollarization in 2000, Ecuador’s GDP has steadily grown, inflation controlled.
en_summary: My take in @eldiario with Francisco Zalles on the dollarization of Ecuador: The Ecuadorian sucre lost 75.6% of its value against the US dollar from 1998 until Jan. 2000, economy imploded. Since dollarization in 2000, Ecuador’s GDP has steadily grown, inflation controlled.
text:
My take in @eldiario with Francisco Zalles on the dollarization of Ecuador:

"The Ecuadorian sucre lost 75.6% of its value against the US dollar from 1998 until Jan. 2000, and the economy imploded. Faced with a currency in free fall, a banking crisis, and an economy in full collapse, Ecuador mothballed the sucre. Since dollarization in 2000, Ecuador’s GDP has steadily grown, inflation has been crushed, and non-oil exports have grown almost twice as fast as GDP."

name: Puru Saxena
zh_summary: @saxena_puru: AI stocks sold off on hotter US inflation (Sept CPI 3.7%) raising odds of more Fed hikes, plus worries over the cost of financing the AI infrastructure buildout.
en_summary: @saxena_puru: AI stocks sold off on hotter US inflation (Sept CPI 3.7%) raising odds of more Fed hikes, plus worries over the cost of financing the AI infrastructure buildout.
text:
AI stocks have sold off over the past few days.

The main drivers: hotter-than-expected US inflation (Sept CPI 3.7% YoY) raising the odds of further Fed hikes, plus growing worries about the cost of financing the massive AI infrastructure buildout. Heavily leveraged names like CoreWeave (roughly $50B in debt/obligations) have been hit especially hard, with bond yields spiking toward 15-16% and credit spreads flashing stress.

Yet the demand picture looks different. Cloud GPU rental prices for high-end chips remain elevated and in several cases, are still trending higher - a real-time signal that compute demand is tight. 

Meanwhile, OpenAI and Anthropic continue scaling: Anthropic just reported $16.8B in Q3 revenue (+45% QoQ), +ve FCF and adjusted profitability, while OpenAI’s net annualised run rate sits around $50B with strong enterprise growth.

This looks more like a rates-and-financing-driven valuation reset than a collapse in underlying AI demand. For investors who believe the secular compute story remains intact, these pullbacks can create selective opportunities - particularly in higher-quality names.
http://alphatarget.com
